role.altitude: The law lecturer keeps talking with prospective students, judging applications, writing moot court problems, speaking at events and advising student boards; answering the same questions by mail, assigning teams and booking rooms by hand shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafted case files into fair moot problems
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer whose routine questions are answered by good pages, leaving time for real conversations.

tasks.short: Let prospective students read the programme FAQ, present at open days, answer remaining questions, review applications, and help place students in internships and clinics to participate in student recruitment, registration and placement activities.

steps.what: Prospective student reads the programme FAQ page before writing
Lecturer presents at open days and talks with prospective students
Lecturer answers prospective students' questions by mail
Lecturer reviews applications for the programme
Student enters placement preferences on the platform form
Lecturer helps place students in internships and legal clinics: collecting preferences from mails into a spreadsheet today, from the platform form list after the change

tasks.design: A programme FAQ page answers the common questions on entry requirements, courses and deadlines, so fewer routine mails reach the lecturer, who answers the rest personally. Open days and reviewing applications stay with people; no software assesses applicants. Students enter placement preferences in a form in the learning platform, and the lecturer arranges placements from that list instead of collecting mails into a spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine questions and preferences arrived by mail.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a hesitant first-generation student to apply.
tasks.altitude: Less routine mail; the people work stays.

evidence.claim: AI used for admission to education is high-risk, so no software assesses applicants here.

assumptions: Boundary: recruitment, registration and placement; advising students on curricula and careers (task 6224) is a sibling task.
Prospective students' time on the FAQ is shown in s1 and is less than writing a mail.

Open days, application review and placement decisions keep their full time. Students' preference entry is shown in s4b. s3 keeps 70 for questions the FAQ does not answer; s5 keeps 70 because arranging placements with hosts stays.
unknowns: Share of questions the FAQ answers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few prospective students read the FAQ first, so s3 keeps 90 (6.2); high: the FAQ takes the routine questions as assumed (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write moot court case files, assign cases and roles for students to hear and try, schedule hearings, and brief students on the case and rules.

steps.what: Lecturer selects or writes the case files for moot court

loop.input: A real judgment chosen by the lecturer and the legal issues to test.
loop.output: A draft fictional case file with changed names and facts that raise the chosen issues.
loop.check: The lecturer checks that each chosen issue arises and that both sides can argue it; no real party names remain.
loop.stop: The lecturer keeps the file, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each problem must be new and balanced.

steps.what: Lecturer assigns cases and roles for students to hear and try
Lecturer schedules hearings and books rooms
Lecturer briefs students on the case and the moot court rules

tasks.design: A drafting step turns a real judgment the lecturer chooses into a fictional case file with changed names and facts, and the lecturer checks that the chosen issues arise and both sides can argue them. Teams and roles are created as groups in the learning platform by fixed rules (each student pleads once for each side), and the lecturer adjusts. Hearings are booked from the timetable's free court rooms. Briefing stays personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problems were written from scratch and teams set in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting from judgments and group tools in learning platforms.
tasks.still_hard: Writing problems that are balanced for both sides.
tasks.human_edge: Designing a problem that makes students think like judges.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and admin; designing and briefing stay.

reach.learn: Whether new problems keep the exercise fresh.

evidence.claim: Drafting course materials is not covered by the AI Act's high-risk education areas.

assumptions: Boundary: assigning moot cases; grading oral presentations (task 6215) is a sibling task.
unknowns: Number of moot rounds per year.
research_questions: Do new problems take less time without being less balanced?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the assignment rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafted case files need much rewriting to make both sides arguable, so s1 keeps 90 (23.2); high: drafts usable after checks as assumed (29.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare a contribution, participate and speak in campus and community events, and arrange logistics with organisers.

steps.what: Lecturer prepares a talk or contribution
Lecturer participates and speaks at campus and community events
Lecturer arranges logistics with the organisers

tasks.design: Talks are adapted from a personal library of earlier slides and notes by topic, and a standard speaker information sheet (bio, photo, technical needs) answers organisers' usual questions. Taking part stays fully personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Talks and speaker details were put together each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Personal slide libraries and speaker sheets.
tasks.still_hard: Events that need a new talk on a new topic.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining law to a community audience without jargon.

reach.learn: Whether speaker details arrive at once.

evidence.claim: Reusing earlier material and a standard speaker sheet shortens preparation.

assumptions: Boundary: campus and community events; consulting for government or industry (task 6236) is a sibling task.
Taking part keeps its full time.

incremental.description: Lecturer files talks in the slide library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: every talk is on a new topic, so nothing from the library is reused and s1 stays 100 (2.8); high: recurring talks adapted from the library as assumed (6.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Let students check the FAQ on rules for organisations, meet and advise the board of student organizations, answer remaining questions, and review and sign event plans and funding applications.

steps.what: Student board member checks the FAQ on rules for student organisations
Lecturer meets with and advises the board of the student organization
Lecturer answers questions on rules, funding and events by mail
Lecturer reviews and signs event plans and funding applications

tasks.design: A short FAQ page with the university's rules for student organisations, funding and events answers the usual questions before they reach the adviser. Advising the board, answering the rest and signing plans stay personal.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same rule questions came in each year with a new board.
tasks.enabler_now: FAQ pages kept by the adviser.
tasks.human_edge: Guiding a new board through its first difficult decision.
assumptions: Boundary: advising student organisations; advising individual students (task 6224) is a sibling task.
Board members' FAQ time is shown in s1 and is less than writing a mail.
Advising and signing keep their full time.

incremental.description: Lecturer updates the FAQ each year.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: board members seldom read the FAQ first, so s3 keeps 90 (1.9); high: the FAQ answers the usual questions as assumed (5.0).
